_what: The fifteen Promptly sound effects as ChatCut project assets, each carrying its MEASURED attack offset. Builder 2, 2026-09-19.
_attack_law: A sound is placed EARLIER than the beat it lands on: start_s = beat_s - attack_ms/1000, clamped at 0. The offset is applied FOR the agent, never asked of it. sfx_start_s() in agentic_editor_app.py is the one implementation.
_lufs_floor: FOUR ENTRIES READ -70.0 LUFS FROM CHATCUT AND ARE NOT SILENT. camera-flash, mouse-click-sound, popsfx and swoosh-sound-effects are all under 400ms, below the EBU R128 integrated gate, so the reader returns its floor. Measured locally: peaks -0.8, -4.5, -5.4 and -0.7 dBFS -- camera-flash and swoosh are within 1 dB of full scale. Recorded as ABSENT_TOO_SHORT, never as a number. Anything that gains, sorts or ducks by integrated_lufs must read the STATE first.
_ours_beside_theirs: These fifteen are OURS, uploaded as project assets. ChatCut's own 36 library sounds (library:sound:*) stay available beside them; this file does not replace or shadow that catalogue.
_transcode: ChatCut transcodes audio to Ogg/Opus on upload, so every asset's filename is <stem>.ogg while the source on disk is <stem>.mp3. The catalogue key is the STEM and is unchanged.

sfx.name: awkward-moment
sfx.role: the story lands on deliberate cringe and holds it — an embarrassing beat recounted or performed, then left sitting (the failed handshake, the reply-all disaster, the joke that died). It belongs just after the line, insid
sfx.fits: viral, comedic, casual storytelling with a held cringe beat — only
sfx.fights: corporate, professional, educational, cinematic — comedic timing has no place in a composed edit

sfx.name: boom
sfx.role: the video's single heaviest claim — the payoff line the whole video was built to deliver, or the one stat that reframes everything before it. It lands on the word that carries the weight
sfx.fits: viral, punchy, high-energy payoffs — the single heaviest hit
sfx.fights: corporate, clean, professional, educational; and cinematic/story climaxes — a boom PUNCHES (sharp attack) where a cinema

sfx.name: camera-flash
sfx.role: a photo or screenshot is taken, shown, or demanded in the content — "screenshot this," "I took one picture," the moment the story itself contains a shutter. The sound IS the shutter the story references
sfx.fits: any vibe — a photo/screenshot literally happening in the content is the gate, not the vibe; the clean snap suits tech/pr
sfx.fights: non-diegetic decoration (never where no shutter happens); its snap is a touch sharp only for a slow, somber beat

sfx.name: imposter
sfx.role: the speaker voices building suspicion — something doesn't add up and they're saying so before the answer arrives ("but something felt off," "turns out he never worked there"). It belongs where the doubt is named
sfx.fits: viral, comedic, casual suspense played for meme-effect — only
sfx.fights: corporate, professional, serious-cinematic — the register reads as a joke; for genuine dramatic suspense, prefer a swell

sfx.name: iphoneding
sfx.role: a message, text, or notification is quoted, shown, or reenacted in the content — the sound IS the notification the story references
sfx.fits: any vibe — a message/notification quoted or shown in the content is the gate; the chime suits casual/viral/tech/product
sfx.fights: non-diegetic filler; a consumer chime is a touch informal only for a formal-corporate or somber-cinematic beat

sfx.name: money-ching
sfx.role: the anchor word itself IS the amount — a number of money, a price, or "free" standing as the price ("$500," "ten grand," "free"). Minutes, hours, and days are TIME words; time words never take the register
sfx.fits: viral, casual, product, hustle — any energetic moment where a price, cost, or "free" lands
sfx.fights: cinematic, story, serious-corporate — reads gimmicky against a polished or emotional register

sfx.name: mouse-click-sound
sfx.role: the speech names a single discrete digital action — "just upload it," "one tap," "hit publish" — where the action's simplicity is the point. It belongs on the spoken action word
sfx.fits: educational, explainer, tech, product-demo, clean-corporate — tactile and informative
sfx.fights: hype/high-energy edits where a quiet click is lost under the energy; comedic registers

sfx.name: popsfx
sfx.role: the speaker stacks a light bonus on top of a point already made — the "oh, and it even does this" beat: small, pleasing, an extra rather than a headline. It belongs on the bonus's landing word
sfx.fits: casual, viral, upbeat — a light bonus
sfx.fights: serious-corporate, cinematic, somber — a cute pop trivializes a weighty or formal beat

sfx.name: punchsfx
sfx.role: the speaker throws a verbal blow — a short, hard declarative that indicts, dismisses, or shuts something down ("that's a scam," "it's dead," "you're doing it wrong"), delivered like a jab, not an explanation. It belongs
sfx.fights: corporate, professional, calm, cinematic — the jab reads as aggression in a composed edit

sfx.name: rizz
sfx.role: the speaker plays charm for comedy — a flirty line, a self-aware flex, a "smooth move" recounted or performed with a wink ("and that's how you get their number"). It belongs where the charm lands
sfx.fits: viral, comedic, casual meme-register charm — only
sfx.fights: corporate, professional, educational, cinematic, story — a meme sting is out of register everywhere serious

sfx.name: shockingsfx
sfx.role: a genuine reversal — the sentence lands somewhere the setup made impossible, or a stat contradicts what the viewer was led to assume. It belongs on the twist word, in a video that actually contains a twist
sfx.fits: viral, dramatic, high-energy reveals and twists
sfx.fights: corporate, professional, calm, educational — a jolt is theatrics in a measured edit

sfx.name: swoosh-sound-effects
sfx.role: the speech itself claims SPEED — a stated how-fast ("in under five minutes," "instantly," "before your coffee's cold") or a rapid-fire run of items delivered at a clip. It belongs on the speed word, or on the takeoff of
sfx.fits: any vibe — the safe motion cue, corporate and educational included; never over-asserts
sfx.fights: nothing tonally; only wrong when there's no motion or speed to voice

sfx.name: transition-sfx
sfx.role: the video's single largest act turn, where a full transition renders — this is the sound of that turn itself
sfx.fits: cinematic, story, professional, educational act-turns; safe on the single biggest turn in any vibe
sfx.fights: nothing tonally; reserved for the ONE largest turn, not scattered

sfx.name: wompwomp
sfx.role: the story reports a failure played for comedy — the attempt flopped and the speaker frames the flop as the punchline ("and it made exactly zero dollars"). It belongs on the fail's landing word
sfx.fits: viral, comedic, casual — a fail played as the punchline; only
sfx.fights: corporate, professional, story, cinematic — trivializes anything earnest

sfx.name: woosh-professional
sfx.role: the narration itself travels — an explicit spoken jump in time or place mid-story ("fast-forward two years," "now come with me to the warehouse," "meanwhile, back at the office"). It belongs on the travel phrase
sfx.fits: any vibe, leans professional/corporate/educational/story — a polished travel cue
